assets.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: product material design reference for a real mechanical instant camera.
Input image 1 is the exact current rear-three-quarter CAD render, the edit target. Image 2 is the user's material and lighting style reference. Image 3 is the existing exact CAMID wordmark identity.
Make a polished rear-view material refinement of image 1. Keep the entire product silhouette, proportions, camera view, all original panels, seams, slot, hinge, crank, levers and holes EXACTLY in place. The product's geometry cannot change. Change only surface finishes, graphic printing and studio lighting.
The rear currently has two broad empty regions. Refine the upper rear shell with a bounded charcoal/graphite satin finish area (a flat finish boundary, not an added plate), a subtle dark-crimson short line, and small carefully aligned 'CAMID B1' and 'MECHANICAL CAMERA' typography near a lower corner. Refine the long lower existing rear door with restrained tactile fine linear micro-rib texture in a central grip area, a fine satin border and a small quiet footer 'B1' / 'LIGHT · MOTION · MEMORY'. The texture must read as refined shallow material grain rather than new grooves or geometry. Keep at least 70 percent of the surface quiet. Red alloy controls stay red; body stays near-black, never red-painted.
CAMID wordmark must preserve the thick condensed angular proportions of image 3 and reference image 2. Do not substitute a generic typeface. Typography is small and purposeful; no giant logo repeated across the back, no fake certifications, serial numbers, screws, ports, screens, windows, carbon-fiber checkerboard, or decorative technical clutter.
Lighting: precision product-release aesthetic, neutral soft key revealing charcoal microtexture, controlled deep crimson rim and a black-red studio background consistent with image 2. Camera should be fully visible and remain the exact same mechanical product. One coherent rear three-quarter product rendering, square composition, high-quality photoreal material look. No labels outside the product, no comparison montage, no watermark.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: product material design reference.
Input image 1 is the exact current left-side three-quarter CAD render and edit target. Image 2 is the user's graphite/crimson style reference. Image 3 is the matching rear finish concept, a style guide only.
Refine image 1's side surface finish. Preserve the exact silhouette, dimensions, camera viewpoint, upper shell, lens, lever slots, crank, side frame, all holes and seams. No new panels, cuts, grips, screws, ports, or hardware.
Apply a fine shallow linear microtexture within the existing long blank lower side face, transitioning to a satin graphite border with a very restrained dark-red line. Treat the wide opposite side of the shutter box as a subtle bounded graphite material region with a compact dark-crimson 'B1' model identifier and small quiet 'MECHANICAL CAMERA' type near the bottom, carefully avoiding existing lever slots. The upper crank-side shell can carry a quiet small 'B1' mark and a short crimson graphic line, not a new mechanism.
This is surface graphics and PBR materials only: charcoal micrograin, satin graphite, fine directional grip texture, existing red brushed-alloy accents, controlled steel reflections, transparent neutral optical glass. At least 70 percent quiet surfaces; minimal product-release precision; complement the rear concept.
Text exact: 'B1', 'MECHANICAL CAMERA'. No fake serial numbers, specifications, certifications, tick scales, or instruction arrows. Do not invent a fake CAMID logo on this side; the established CAMID logo remains on the other side.
Lighting: neutral soft key that reveals grain, deep crimson rim, restrained black-red product studio, photoreal refined industrial design. Single square full-product image, no external labels, no collage, no watermark.

Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: FLAT UV BASE-COLOR TEXTURE, not a product rendering.
Use the attached rear-camera concept only for surface design style. Generate a clean flat, front-on rectangular charcoal rear-door finish texture, portrait aspect 2:3, ideally 1024x1536. The image itself is the texture and must fill the entire frame edge to edge, with NO camera, NO perspective, NO border outside the image, NO light gradient, NO cast shadow, NO baked specular, NO ambient studio background, NO 3D thickness.
Layout: near-black fine-grain polymer outer margin 6%; a shallow horizontal fine linear grip grain occupies x=10..90%, y=6..85%, same dark charcoal color; keep ribs subtle, dense and nearly flush, no deep grooves. A hairline satin graphite boundary delineates this grain area. Footer y=87..96% remains quiet fine bead-blasted graphite and contains a SMALL left-aligned grey 'B1' at x=12%, followed on the next line by tiny tracked exact 'LIGHT · MOTION · MEMORY'. Leave the right half footer empty. No CAMID logo on this door, no red paint on this map, no screws, no ports, no fake serials, no extra symbols.
Use charcoal RGB approximately 31,33,36 for the outer polymer, graphite 39,42,45 for the grip face, slightly brighter neutral graphite for the hairline border. Grain is low contrast, physically plausible. Footer text grey RGB approx 125,125,128. This is a restrained precision product texture sheet with crisp small typography, even illumination and no scene.

Use case: product-mockup. Asset type: FLAT UV BASE-COLOR TEXTURE, not a product rendering.
Use the attached camera side concept for surface design style. Generate a flat long rectangular side grip texture, portrait aspect 1:2.4, ideally 1024x2432. Fill image edge to edge with the material atlas; no camera, no perspective, no 3D thickness, no cast shadows, no baked highlights, no gradient or surrounding background.
The outermost 8% is near-black micrograin polymer. A long very shallow fine horizontal linear grain occupies x=15..88%, y=8..78%, quietly darker than a satin graphite thin perimeter. At x=12%, a short restrained hairline dark-crimson vertical stripe runs from y=10% to 82%. The footer at y=83..94% has small bold compact exact 'B1' in dark crimson and tiny widely tracked grey 'MECHANICAL CAMERA' below it, aligned left to x=18%, leaving ample empty space. Keep all typography small and readable. Dense subtle grain, no thick ribs, no embossed bevels. At least 70 percent quiet dark texture. No CAMID logo, serials, ports, fake certifications or instruction arrows.
Charcoal palette RGB 27,29,32 with graphite differences no more than 12 RGB levels; crimson accents RGB around 115,28,34; footer grey about 100,101,103. Even flat illumination, clean precision product-release surface artwork.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: FLAT UV BASE-COLOR TEXTURE for the rear of a mechanical instant camera's upper shell.
Input image 1 is the exact approved CAMID wordmark artwork: retain its thick condensed angular letter silhouettes and dark-red color. Input image 2 is the rear material concept, for layout and texture reference only.
Create an edge-to-edge front-on wide flat graphite finish texture sheet, aspect ratio 2.35:1, ideally 1536x656. No product, no camera, no perspective, no light gradient, no baked shadows/highlights or 3D bevels. It must be usable directly as a PBR base color map.
Background: restrained charcoal fine bead-blasted polymer RGB around 34,36,39, subtle surface variation only. Thin satin graphite boundary inset 5% from all edges, no actual panel gap. In the lower right area, at x=66..88%, y=62..79%, reproduce exact small dark-crimson CAMID from input 1, preserving all letter shapes and proportions; a grey compact 'B1' follows it. Directly below, tiny wide-tracked exact 'MECHANICAL CAMERA'. A short hairline dark-crimson horizontal stroke sits to the left of the wordmark at x=48..62%, y=68%. Keep upper 60% and left 45% almost entirely quiet. The center lower edge must be empty so a real central hinge does not cover typography.
No extra typography, fake certifications, serial numbers, screws, embossing, geometry or surrounding background. Brand identity consistent with the given artwork. Texture itself fills the entire image, even flat illumination.
